findings.excerpt: If each q_{n,j}->$p_j$ ... Its empirical integral is q_{n,j} ... weak convergence implies q_{n,j}->$p_j$.
findings.symptom: The frequency symbol q_{n,j} and convergence arrow are emitted as literal ASCII text in the rendered proof, while neighboring p_j expressions are typeset. The rendered formula therefore has an unformatted subscript and -> arrow.
findings.suggested_repair: Typeset both frequency occurrences consistently, for example $q_{n,j}	o p_j$, including the sentence identifying the empirical integral.

editorial_candidates.excerpt: The two-state identity chain has invariant law (1/2,1/2), two absorbing states, and a strictly shift-invariant event with probability 1/2.
editorial_candidates.rationale: A two-node state diagram would make the counterexample immediate: each state has only a self-loop, so paths stay at their initial state and the initial mixture remains visible. The source fully specifies all vertices, transition edges, and weights.
editorial_candidates.labels_and_relations_to_draw_or_check: Draw nodes 0 and 1, a probability-one self-loop at each, and no edge between them. Mark initial mass 1/2 at each node. If a path-space annotation is included, show the supported constant paths (0,0,...) and (1,1,...) and the event selecting the first path with mass 1/2. Do not imply irreducibility.

editorial_candidates.excerpt: X_t(ω)=0 and Y_t(ω)=1_{U=t}(ω); each Y path has a single spike at t=ω, and the simultaneous-equality event is empty.
editorial_candidates.rationale: The distinction between pointwise modifications and pathwise indistinguishability is the central contrast, and one path plot can communicate it much faster than the epsilon-delta argument. The source determines the complete path shapes and endpoint behavior.
editorial_candidates.labels_and_relations_to_draw_or_check: For one fixed ω∈[0,1], plot time t∈[0,1], X_t(ω)=0 as the zero line, and Y_t(ω)=1 at t=ω and 0 elsewhere; label the isolated spike and indicate that the same construction applies for interior and endpoint ω. State in the caption that every fixed t has P(U=t)=0, while for every ω the two paths differ at t=ω, so no sample path pair is identical.

editorial_candidates.excerpt: A connected locally finite bipartite graph has simple random walk with every vertex of period two; each edge crosses the two parts and a neighbor backtrack gives a two-step return.
editorial_candidates.rationale: A graph schematic naturally presents the defining bipartition, alternating support, and positive two-step return that establish the period claim. All shown relations are explicitly required by the source.
editorial_candidates.labels_and_relations_to_draw_or_check: Draw an illustrative connected bipartite graph with V_0 and V_1 in separate columns or colors, x_0∈V_0 adjacent to z∈V_1, and the backtrack x_0→z→x_0. Show an arbitrary graph path alternating sides and label odd-time support in V_1 and even-time support in V_0. Mark that there are no within-part edges and that connectivity transfers the period to every y; avoid implying the graph is finite or that all paths have a fixed length.
